edges.reason: Both statements report that two airports in Saudi Arabia were damaged. They are from different WSJ articles with different reporting sources (one citing the kingdom, the other being the outlet's own reporting on claimed attacks).

edges.label: same_fact
edges.reason: Both occurrences report that two Saudi airports (specifically those in Jazan and Najran) were damaged in Houthi attacks. Both are from The Wall Street Journal and cite the Saudi government/authority.

edges.sentence: On 2026-10-07, The Wall Street Journal reported “Attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels damaged two airports in southern Saudi Arabia near the border with the war-torn nation, the kingdom said Tuesday, marking the latest escalation in fighting that threatens global energy markets.”; on 2026-10-08, The Wall Street Journal reported “Attacks claimed by Houthi militants damaged two airports in Saudi Arabia.”.

On 2026-10-07, The Wall Street Journal reported “King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport were damaged in attacks”; on 2026-10-08, The Wall Street Journal reported “Attacks claimed by Houthi militants damaged two airports in Saudi Arabia.”.

On 2026-10-07, The Wall Street Journal reported “King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport were damaged in attacks”; on the same day, The Wall Street Journal reported “Attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels damaged two airports in southern Saudi Arabia near the border with the war-torn nation, the kingdom said Tuesday, marking the latest escalation in fighting that threatens global energy markets.”.
